en.title: I Know Whom I Have Believed
en.author: Daniel W. Whittle
stanzas:
[D]I know not why God's [G]wondrous [D]grace
To me He hath made [A]known,
[A7]Nor [D]why, unworthy, [G]Christ in [D]love
Re[A]deemed me for [A7]His [D]own.

I know not how this saving faith
To me He did impart,
Nor how believing in His Word
Wrought peace within my heart.

I know not how the Spirit moves,
Convincing men of sin,
Revealing Jesus through the Word,
Creating faith in Him.

I know not what of good or ill
May be reserved for me,
Of weary ways or golden days,
Before His face I see.

I know not when my Lord may come,
At night or noonday fair,
Nor if I walk the vale with Him,
Or meet Him in the air.
en.chorus:
But "I [G]know Whom I have be[D]lieved,
And am per[A7]suaded that He is [D]able
To [G]keep that which I've com[D]mitted
Unto [A7]Him against that [D]day."

notes: Text from Timeless Truths (Hymns for His Praise No. 2, 1906), five stanzas. The Cyber Hymnal's transcription of Gospel Hymns No. 4 (1883) agrees except that it reads 'Convincing us of sin' in stanza 3 and marks 'believèd'; hymnary's representative text (Our Great Redeemer's Praise) prints four stanzas (stanza 4 'what of good or ill' dropped) and reads 'convicting men of sin'. 'Convincing men' is the 1883 reading and ships. Tune EL NATHAN (James McGranahan, 1883), meter 8.6.8.6 with refrain (hymnary's tune record writes the refrain out as 8.6.8.6.9.10.8.7). Key D: hymnary's instances run 40 D to 19 E-flat; TT prints D, already a guitar key. Chords derived from the Timeless Truths MusicXML score by reading the four-part chord on every beat. The stanza is I with IV/D and diminished neighbours over the tonic pedal, of which the IV on 'wondrous' and 'Christ' is kept and the rest dropped; the vi-V7 approach under 'made' was dropped; 'Redeemed me for His own' is V-V7-I. Refrain: IV-I, V7-I (a ii7 before 'able' dropped), IV-I, then V7 with a one-beat VI (B major, V of ii) dropped, I.
